title: Security appliances software versions MX 26.1.7 changelog

announcements.post_subject: A new Recommended Release MX Security & SD-WAN firmware is now available

Executive summary: MX 26.1.7 is the first Recommended release in the MX 26.1 release family.
We recommend planned, phased production adoption in accordance with normal change-control and platform-compatibility guidance.
VPN and SD-WAN fixes improve Auto VPN throughput, tunnel recovery, and SD-WAN policy recovery.
Routing and switching fixes improve VLAN configuration recovery and platform-specific port behaviour.
Bug fixes - general fixes: Fixed an issue that could prevent IKEv1 IPsec Client VPN users from communicating with hosts reachable through Auto VPN. (MX-52259)
Preserved IPv6 Traffic Class markings for traffic carried over Auto VPN. (MX-52047)
Resolved an issue that could prevent SD-WAN statistics from populating and policies from applying after an Auto VPN contact port changed on a passthrough-mode appliance. (MX-44815)
Resolved an issue that could prevent Auto VPN tunnels from forming after an HA failover when WAN virtual IPs were not configured. (MX-53131)
Fixed an issue that could allow IPv4 limited broadcast and multicast traffic in VRFs other than the default VRF to follow the default route instead of being discarded. (MX-52095)
Restored downstream IPv6 connectivity after WAN link interruptions or upstream network changes for MX appliances using DHCPv6 Prefix Delegation. (MX-50008)
Resolved an issue that could cause an unexpected restart when an appliance learned unusually large numbers of source MAC addresses. (MX-51082)
Stopped repeated DNS service restarts when the appliance remained on an IPv6-only uplink. (MX-44620)
Fixed an issue that could cause the Local Status Page to become unavailable after processing a malformed request. (MX-52203)

As part of Cisco's ongoing commitment to proactive security and product quality, the MX engineering team has conducted a comprehensive internal security review. This review resulted in one or more software hardening release(s) that address(e)s multiple internally discovered vulnerabilities.
Bug fixes - limited platform fixes: Fixed an issue that caused SNMP LAN port traffic counters to report zero on C8111-G2-MX and C8121-G2-MX secure routers. (MX-51167)
Fixed an issue on C8111-G2-MX and C8121-G2-MX secure routers that could cause a connected switch port to block traffic when MX LAN ports used a mix of trunk and access configurations. (MX-46286)

Fixed issues affecting Ethernet link-speed configuration on C8355-G2-MX secure routers, including unsupported Local Status Page options, manual speeds not being applied, and LAN ports negotiating at higher speeds than configured. (MX-42602, MX-50742, MX-50015)
Fixed an issue on C8455-G2-MX and C8355-G2-MX secure routers that could prevent converted SFP uplinks from forwarding spanning-tree control traffic after being changed back to LAN ports. (MX-50759)
Fixed an issue that could allow PoE to remain enabled on C8355-G2-MX secure routers when a PoE-capable power adapter was not connected. (MX-50388)
Resolved an issue that could reduce Auto VPN TCP throughput on MX67, MX68, MX75, MX85, and Z-series appliances over higher-latency VPN paths. (MX-48759)
Resolved an issue that could reduce Auto VPN TCP throughput on MX95 and MX105 appliances over higher-latency VPN paths when Intrusion Detection and Prevention was set to Prevention mode. (MX-49287)
Resolved an issue that could delay restoration of connectivity on MX95, MX105, MX250, and MX450 appliances while large VLAN configurations were being applied. (MX-45337, MX-49962)
Fixed an issue that could prevent C8121-G2-MX, MX95, and MX105 appliances from loading forwarding configuration after downgrading from MX 26.2 to MX 26.1. (MX-52861)
Fixed an issue that could leave the Local Status Page unavailable and cause an additional restart during startup on MX95 and MX105 appliances. (MX-52511)
Fixed an issue that could cause MX450 appliances to restart unexpectedly when firewall policies were updated. (MX-51567)
Legacy products notice: When configured for this version, Z3(C) devices will run MX 19.2.8.
When configured for this version, MX64(W), MX65(W), MX84, MX100, and vMX100 devices will run MX 18.107.13.
Known issues: Networks configured with legacy IPv4 manual inbound firewall rules but no NAT Exceptions may have those rules hidden after upgrading to Wired 26.1.3 or later. Add a NAT Exception before making further configuration changes to avoid losing the rules. See NAT Exceptions documentation for more info.
On MX appliances in HA with a virtual IP, configuring an IPsec VPN peer to use multiple WAN uplinks may prevent all IPsec VPN tunnels from establishing. (MX-49849)
On MX 26.1 appliances, Auto VPN tunnels may fail to establish over WAN 3 when it is the only active uplink and a peer is running firmware earlier than MX 26.1. (MX-50123)
When IPsec VPN over multiple WAN uplinks is enabled, IKEv1 Client VPN connections may fail if upstream NAT changes the client's IKE source port from UDP 500. (MX-51712)
DNS resolution may fail for clients on a VLAN configured to use “Proxy upstream DNS” when the VLAN is bound to a Group Policy that denies traffic to the same VLAN subnet. (MX-47367)
Other: The product complies with EN 18031-1:2024 and EN 18031-2: 2024

Security appliances software versions MX 26.1.7 changelog

Executive summary

  • MX 26.1.7 is the first Recommended release in the MX 26.1 release family.

  • We recommend planned, phased production adoption in accordance with normal change-control and platform-compatibility guidance.

  • VPN and SD-WAN fixes improve Auto VPN throughput, tunnel recovery, and SD-WAN policy recovery.

  • Routing and switching fixes improve VLAN configuration recovery and platform-specific port behaviour.

Bug fixes - general fixes

  • Fixed an issue that could prevent IKEv1 IPsec Client VPN users from communicating with hosts reachable through Auto VPN. (MX-52259)

  • Preserved IPv6 Traffic Class markings for traffic carried over Auto VPN. (MX-52047)

  • Resolved an issue that could prevent SD-WAN statistics from populating and policies from applying after an Auto VPN contact port changed on a passthrough-mode appliance. (MX-44815)

  • Resolved an issue that could prevent Auto VPN tunnels from forming after an HA failover when WAN virtual IPs were not configured. (MX-53131)

  • Fixed an issue that could allow IPv4 limited broadcast and multicast traffic in VRFs other than the default VRF to follow the default route instead of being discarded. (MX-52095)

  • Restored downstream IPv6 connectivity after WAN link interruptions or upstream network changes for MX appliances using DHCPv6 Prefix Delegation. (MX-50008)

  • Resolved an issue that could cause an unexpected restart when an appliance learned unusually large numbers of source MAC addresses. (MX-51082)

  • Stopped repeated DNS service restarts when the appliance remained on an IPv6-only uplink. (MX-44620)

  • Fixed an issue that could cause the Local Status Page to become unavailable after processing a malformed request. (MX-52203)

  • As part of Cisco's ongoing commitment to proactive security and product quality, the MX engineering team has conducted a comprehensive internal security review. This review resulted in one or more software hardening release(s) that address(e)s multiple internally discovered vulnerabilities.

Bug fixes - limited platform fixes

  • Fixed an issue that caused SNMP LAN port traffic counters to report zero on C8111-G2-MX and C8121-G2-MX secure routers. (MX-51167)

  • Fixed an issue on C8111-G2-MX and C8121-G2-MX secure routers that could cause a connected switch port to block traffic when MX LAN ports used a mix of trunk and access configurations. (MX-46286)

  • Fixed issues affecting Ethernet link-speed configuration on C8355-G2-MX secure routers, including unsupported Local Status Page options, manual speeds not being applied, and LAN ports negotiating at higher speeds than configured. (MX-42602, MX-50742, MX-50015)

  • Fixed an issue on C8455-G2-MX and C8355-G2-MX secure routers that could prevent converted SFP uplinks from forwarding spanning-tree control traffic after being changed back to LAN ports. (MX-50759)

  • Fixed an issue that could allow PoE to remain enabled on C8355-G2-MX secure routers when a PoE-capable power adapter was not connected. (MX-50388)

  • Resolved an issue that could reduce Auto VPN TCP throughput on MX67, MX68, MX75, MX85, and Z-series appliances over higher-latency VPN paths. (MX-48759)

  • Resolved an issue that could reduce Auto VPN TCP throughput on MX95 and MX105 appliances over higher-latency VPN paths when Intrusion Detection and Prevention was set to Prevention mode. (MX-49287)

  • Resolved an issue that could delay restoration of connectivity on MX95, MX105, MX250, and MX450 appliances while large VLAN configurations were being applied. (MX-45337, MX-49962)

  • Fixed an issue that could prevent C8121-G2-MX, MX95, and MX105 appliances from loading forwarding configuration after downgrading from MX 26.2 to MX 26.1. (MX-52861)

  • Fixed an issue that could leave the Local Status Page unavailable and cause an additional restart during startup on MX95 and MX105 appliances. (MX-52511)

  • Fixed an issue that could cause MX450 appliances to restart unexpectedly when firewall policies were updated. (MX-51567)

Legacy products notice

  • When configured for this version, Z3(C) devices will run MX 19.2.8.

  • When configured for this version, MX64(W), MX65(W), MX84, MX100, and vMX100 devices will run MX 18.107.13.

Known issues

  • Networks configured with legacy IPv4 manual inbound firewall rules but no NAT Exceptions may have those rules hidden after upgrading to Wired 26.1.3 or later. Add a NAT Exception before making further configuration changes to avoid losing the rules. See NAT Exceptions documentation for more info.

  • On MX appliances in HA with a virtual IP, configuring an IPsec VPN peer to use multiple WAN uplinks may prevent all IPsec VPN tunnels from establishing. (MX-49849)

  • On MX 26.1 appliances, Auto VPN tunnels may fail to establish over WAN 3 when it is the only active uplink and a peer is running firmware earlier than MX 26.1. (MX-50123)

  • When IPsec VPN over multiple WAN uplinks is enabled, IKEv1 Client VPN connections may fail if upstream NAT changes the client's IKE source port from UDP 500. (MX-51712)

  • DNS resolution may fail for clients on a VLAN configured to use “Proxy upstream DNS” when the VLAN is bound to a Group Policy that denies traffic to the same VLAN subnet. (MX-47367)

  • The product complies with EN 18031-1:2024 and EN 18031-2: 2024
